title: Nondeterministic polynomial time implies BPP
statement: For every rational-valued function $p$ on input lengths and every language $L$ of bit strings, if $L$ has a nondeterministic polynomial-time machine that halts on every choice string of the prescribed polynomial length and outputs the correct membership bit with probability at least $p(n)$, then there is a polynomial-time randomized verifier that outputs the correct membership bit with probability at least $p(n)$ on every input of length $n$.
